stories.statLabel: monthly TV fee to be scrapped
stories.headline: Tens of thousands rally in Prague for public media
body: Tens of thousands protested in Prague against plans to change how public media is funded.
PM Andrej Babiš wants state-budget funding instead of a household fee.
Critics say that would give the government more control.
stories.joke: Bedtime stories, now with political subplots.
stories.vc: State-funded media can lose ad and audience trust if seen as less independent.

stories.headline: Record migrant arrivals push Spain to declare emergency in Canary Islands
body: Over 9,000 people have reached the Canary Islands since November began.
Rescuers saved 1,488 people from 14 boats on Saturday, a one-day record.
Spain has declared a migration emergency.
stories.vc: Spain will need more EU money for reception and rescue.

stories.headline: Netanyahu pushes Eisenkot for a unity government
body: Caretaker PM Benjamin Netanyahu is urging opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a unity government.
Eisenkot, who has the first chance to form a government, called the appeal a 'bluff'.
Their parties are still holding talks.
stories.joke: Nice try, says the man with the mandate.
stories.vc: A stable government would reassure investors in Israel's tech sector.

stories.headline: US floats NATO path for Ukraine if it gives up Donbas
body: Zelenskyy says US envoys offered Ukraine a route to NATO if it gives up all of Donbas.
Russia's Putin has demanded the region; Kyiv has refused to cede land.
Witkoff and Kushner then met Putin in Moscow.
stories.vc: Any peace deal would open a huge rebuilding market in Ukraine.

stories.headline: India's public health spending tripled in a decade
body: Union government health spending rose to ₹4.14 lakh crore in 2023-24 from ₹1.30 lakh crore in 2013-14.
Families' out-of-pocket share fell from 64.2% to 42.7%.
The figures come from new National Health Accounts estimates.
stories.joke: Your wallet finally gets a little rest.
stories.vc: More public spending widens the market for hospitals that serve government schemes.

stories.headline: EaseMyTrip almost breaks even as revenue jumps 34%
body: EaseMyTrip's Q2 loss shrank 98% to ₹56.5 lakh.
Operating revenue rose 33.5% to ₹157.9 crore.
Gross bookings grew 25.5% to ₹2,458 crore.
stories.joke: Almost profitable, the travel version of 'almost there'.
stories.vc: Better numbers could revive investor interest in listed travel stocks.

stories.headline: ED arrests Mahadev betting app promoter after extradition
body: The ED arrested Mahadev app promoter Saurabh Chandrakar after he was extradited from Oman.
The CBI searched 33 places across six states.
It seized phones and papers pointing to mule bank accounts and hawala networks.
stories.vc: The crackdown signals tougher action on illegal betting money flows.

stories.headline: V-Xpress expands logistics hubs around Bengaluru
body: Cargo firm V-Xpress will open over 15 outlets across Karnataka, creating more than 150 jobs.
It is targeting Bengaluru and industrial clusters like Narasapura and Dabaspet.
It is pitching scheduled delivery to quick-commerce sellers.
stories.joke: Your 10-minute delivery needs a 10-hour truck first.
stories.vc: Quick commerce is pulling logistics investment into Karnataka.

stories.headline: Microsoft's email outage became a global cloud crisis
body: A day-long Microsoft outage spread from Outlook and Teams to cloud files, Copilot and Defender.
It began in the Americas and spread worldwide.
Microsoft said many servers became unexpectedly unavailable.
stories.joke: Have you tried turning the cloud off and on again?
stories.vc: Outages strengthen the case for businesses spreading work across several clouds.

stories.headline: Uber says hackers stole drivers' licence data via a tech supplier
body: Uber is telling thousands of drivers their licence details were stolen in an October breach at a supplier.
TechCrunch says the supplier is AI firm Fireworks AI.
Notion's data was also taken in the same hack.
stories.joke: Your AI vendor's password is now your problem.
stories.vc: Supplier hacks are making AI startups prove their security before winning big clients.
